references.text: The preceding verse describes the situation where someone opens a well and an animal falls into it, establishing liability for the owner of the well.
Concerns compensation for damage to another's property, with the same principle of full restitution (יְשַׁלֵּם) for loss.
A similar principle of restitution applies when a borrowed animal dies or is injured, and the owner keeps the dead animal.
The principle of replacing life for life regarding animals: whoever kills an animal must replace it.
A parallel law on compensation when an ox injures another ox, with the same principle that the dead animal goes to the one who must pay restitution.
Both verses establish the principle of financial compensation for animal death in contrast to the death penalty for killing a person.
Both verses set forth the obligation of full restitution when a hired animal dies without the owner being present.
